He is currently a coach, most recently working as the associate head coach for the [[Birmingham Squadron|Erie BayHawks]] of the [[NBA G League]]. Vásquez also represented the [[Venezuela men's national basketball team|Venezuela national team]] in international competitions, as he was born in [[Caracas]] and moved to the United States to attend high school at [[Montrose Christian School]] in [[Rockville, Maryland]] in 2004.Tysiac, Ken. [http://www.sportingnews.com/yourturn/viewtopic.php?t=311763 "Q&A with Maryland guard Greivis Vásquez"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071220224213/http://www.sportingnews.com/yourturn/viewtopic.php?t=311763 |date=2007-12-20 }}, ''[[Sporting News]]'', November 29, 2007. Accessed December 1, 2007. "Q: What was Kevin Durant like when you played with him at Montrose Christian?" During his senior year at Montrose he committed to the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]] to play under head coach [[Gary Williams]]. He was drafted in 2010 after a U.S. [[College basketball|college]] career with [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]], where he finished second on the Terrapins' all-time scoring list with 2,171 career points.[https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4291/greivis-vasquez Greivis Vásquez stats] In 2007, Vásquez played on the [[Venezuela national basketball team]] in the FIBA America Championships. In his final college season of [[2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2009–10]], he was one of three Venezuelans playing in [[NCAA Division I]] men's basketball, with the others being [[David Cubillan]] of the [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette Golden Eagles]] and [[Gregory Echenique]] of the [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton Bluejays]]. ==Early life== Vásquez grew up in [[Caracas]], Venezuela, where he lived with his parents, Ivis Rodriguez and Gregorio Vásquez, and brother, Ingerman Sanoya. His first name is a portmanteau of his parents' first names. After an impressive youth career in his country where he also led the Venezuelan U-15 National Team to the FIBA U-15 South American Championship title in 2003, he was selected to participate at the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]]'s [[Basketball Without Borders]] camp (2004) being a headliner at the event. He started to garner international attention and accepted a scholarship to continue his development in Maryland. At Montrose Christian, Vásquez played under head coach Stu Vetter, and helped the Mustangs post a 43–5 record over his junior and senior seasons. While at Montrose Christian he played for coach Stu Vetter with future NBA star [[Kevin Durant]]. {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2006}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Greivis Vásquez | position = [[Shooting guard|SG]] | hometown = Caracas, Venezuela | highschool = [[Montrose Christian School]] | feet = 6 | inches = 5.25 | weight = 177 | 40 = | commitdate = 2005-11-09 | rivals stars = 4 | scout stars = 4 | espn grade = }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2006 | rivals ref title = Maryland 2006 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = 2006 Maryland Basketball Commits | espn ref title = | rivals school = | scout s = | espn schoolid = | scout overall = NR, 25 ([[Shooting guard|SG]]) | rivals overall = 46, 10 (SG) | espn overall = | access-date = 2012-07-12 | bball = yes }} ==College career== [[Image:Greivis Vasquez (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright=1.1|Vásquez introduced during [[Midnight Madness (basketball)|Midnight Madness]] in 2009]] ===Freshman year (2006–07)=== In the beginning of his freshman year (2006–07), Vásquez did not start for the Terps, but still played solid minutes. Midway through the season, he began starting at the [[2 guard]] position, alongside fellow freshman Eric Hayes at the starting [[point guard]] position. He remained a starter for the rest of the season. He heavily contributed to the Terrapins' six-game winning streak at the end of the season, giving Maryland a #4 seed in the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]]. Vásquez averaged 9.8 points, 4.7 assists and 3.3 rebounds per game during his freshman season, and shooting percentages of 44.4 for field goals, 31.6 for three-pointers and 79.8 for free throws. ===Sophomore year (2007–08)=== Vásquez had per-game averages of 17 points, 6.8 assists and 5.7 rebounds, and shooting percentages of 43.2 for field goals, 30.9 for three-pointers and 78.2 for free throws. ===Junior year (2008–09)=== As a junior, Vásquez led the Terrapins in scoring (17.5), rebounds (5.4), assists (5.0), steals (1.4), and minutes (34.6) per game. He became the first Terrapin basketball player to ever lead the team in points, rebounds and assists in a single season, and only the sixth to accomplish that task in the ACC. On February 21, 2009, Vásquez registered a then career-high 35 points, and 11 rebounds and 10 assists—Maryland's third [[triple-double]] in history and the first since 1987—in a come-from-behind 88–85 overtime win over [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20121106220150/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290520120 Vásquez records triple-double to lead Maryland's rally past No. 3 UNC]{{cite news|url=http://www.interbasket.net/news/1072/2009/02/21/greivis-vasquez-maryland-shocks-3-north-carolina|title=Greivis Vásquez, Maryland upsets North Carolina|publisher=Interbasket.net|date=February 21, 2009}} At the end of his junior year, Vásquez ranked seventh in scoring, third in free throw percentage (.867), third in assists per game, third in assist-to-turnover ratio (1.80) and fifth in minutes per game in the ACC. He reached double figures in scoring in 57 of his last 61 games, including each of his last 17. In Maryland's final ten games, he recorded five 20-point games.{{cite news|url=http://www.umterps.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/vasquez_greivis00.html|title=Greivis Vásquez Basketball Profile|publisher=UMTerps.com|access-date=2009-11-16|archive-date=2008-07-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080705120307/http://www.umterps.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/vasquez_greivis00.html|url-status=dead}} Vásquez was named to the All-ACC second team at the close of the regular season.{{cite news|url=http://weblogs.baltimoresun.com/sports/college/maryland_terps/blog/2009/03/greivis_named_secondteam_allacc.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090313061838/http://weblogs.baltimoresun.com/sports/college/maryland_terps/blog/2009/03/greivis_named_secondteam_allacc.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 13, 2009|title=Greivis Vásquez named second-team All-ACC|publisher=baltimoresun.com}} After the season, Vásquez participated in NBA workouts, where he received mostly positive feedback from professional scouts. He twice met with coach Gary Williams and his Montrose Christian coach, Stu Vetter, to discuss his future. Three hours before the deadline, Vásquez withdrew his name from the [[NBA draft]] in order to return to Maryland for his senior season. Williams said, "He talked to about 14 or 15 teams and really got a good feel for his situation. I think he's made a great move. He returns as possibly the best guard in the ACC and one of the best guards in the country."Steve Yanda, [https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2009/06/15/AR2009061502804.html Terrapins Guard Greivis Vasquez Withdraws From NBA Draft, Will Return to Maryland for Senior Season], ''The Washington Post'', June 16, 2009. [[File:Greivis 2009.jpg|thumb|center|650px|Greivis Vásquez brings the ball upcourt during the [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Terrapins']] 88–85 victory over [[North Carolina men's basketball|North Carolina]] on February 21, 2009. Vasquez had 35 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists in the game.]] ===Senior year (2009–10)=== As a senior, Vásquez averaged 19.6 points, 6.3 assists, 4.6 rebounds and 1.7 steals per game over 33 games. Vásquez was the only player in the country to average more than 18 points and 6 assists per game. His honors included the 2010 [[Bob Cousy Award]] given by the [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame]] to the nation's best collegiate point guard, for which he edged out [[Sherron Collins]] (Kansas), [[Scottie Reynolds]] (Villanova), [[Jon Scheyer]] (Duke), [[Evan Turner]] (Ohio State) and [[John Wall]] (Kentucky).{{cite news| url=http://voices.washingtonpost.com/terrapins-insider/2010/03/vasquez_named_one_of_six_cousy.html | archive-url=https://archive.today/20120718230759/http://voices.washingtonpost.com/terrapins-insider/2010/03/vasquez_named_one_of_six_cousy.html | url-status=dead | archive-date=July 18, 2012 | newspaper=The Washington Post | title=Vásquez named one of six Cousy Award finalists | access-date=May 4, 2010}} Against [[2009–10 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|Georgia Tech]] on February 20, 2010, Vásquez scored the 2,000th point of his collegiate career, making him the only player in ACC history to compile at least 2,000 points, 700 assists and 600 rebounds.{{cite news|url=http://www.wtop.com/?nid=177&sid=1893484|title=Maryland squeezes past Georgia Tech 76–74 |last=Ginsburg|first=David|date=February 20, 2010|agency=Associated Press|access-date=February 21, 2010}} The following week, Vásquez set a new career scoring high with 41 points in the Terrapins' double-overtime victory at [[2009–10 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team|Virginia Tech]].{{cite news|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2010/02/28/terps-outlast-va-tech-in-double-overtime/|title=Terps outlast Va. Tech in double overtime|publisher=Baltimore Sun|date=February 27, 2010}} Vásquez also scored 20 points in Maryland's home win over [[2009–10 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] on Senior Night, and made several critical baskets and assists in the final minutes to secure a victory. Vásquez helped lead Maryland to a 13–3 conference record to tie Duke for the regular season ACC championship. He was named a unanimous first-team All-ACC selection on March 8, 2010, and the [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|ACC Player of the Year]] on March 9, 2010, beating out Duke's [[Jon Scheyer]] and Virginia Tech's [[Malcolm Delaney]].{{cite news|url=http://www.theacc.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030810aac.html|title=ACC Announces 2009–10 All-ACC (2010–2011)=== [[File:Greivis Vasquez at draft night.jpg|thumb|right|Vásquez after being selected in the 2010 NBA draft]] The [[Memphis Grizzlies]] selected Vásquez with the 28th pick in the first round of the [[2010 NBA draft]], using one of the picks traded from the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] via the [[Pau Gasol]] trade.[https://web.archive.org/web/20120928232337/http://voices.washingtonpost.com/dcsportsbog/2010/06/greivis_vasquez_drafted_celebr.html Greivis Vásquez drafted, celebration begins], ''The Washington Post'', June 24, 2010. Throughout the regular season of his rookie year, Vásquez received spot minutes and scored in double digits only twice, but he gained extensive playing time in the [[2011 NBA Playoffs]].[http://weblogs.baltimoresun.com/sports/thetoydepartment/2011/04/without_shimmies_vasquez_shine.html Without shimmies, Vásquez shines on big stage] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110504114611/http://weblogs.baltimoresun.com/sports/thetoydepartment/2011/04/without_shimmies_vasquez_shine.html |date=2011-05-04 }}, ''The Baltimore Sun'', April 30, 2011. Memphis faced the first-seeded [[San Antonio Spurs]] in the first round, where the Grizzlies won their first postseason game in franchise history. In Game Four, Vásquez substituted for starting point guard [[Mike Conley Jr.]], who had gotten into foul trouble. During his 13 minutes of playing time, he had nine points and two assists as Memphis won, 104–86. Memphis advanced to meet the four-seeded [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in the Conference Semifinals, where Vásquez faced off with his former Montrose Christian classmate, [[Kevin Durant]].[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/wizards/kevin-durant-greivis-vasquez-will-play-their-roles--against-each-other--in-nba-playoffs/2011/04/30/AFLio7NF_story.html Kevin Durant, Greivis Vásquez will play their roles — against each other — in NBA playoffs], ''The Washington Post'', April 30, 2011. The Thunder would win the series. In the 2011 offseason, Vásquez took part in a [[United States State Department]] sponsored trip to his native Venezuela to hold clinics and meet with sports officials.{{cite news|last=Frommer|first=Frederic|title=Vazquez, State Dept. team up on trip to Venezuela|url=http://www.seattlepi.com/sports/article/Vazquez-State-Dept-team-up-on-trip-to-Venezuela-1424981.php|access-date=16 June 2011|newspaper=Seattle Post-Intelligencer|date=15 June 2011}}{{cite news|last=Van Valkenburg|first=Kevin|title=Greivis Vasquez: NBA player, sports diplomat|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2011/06/15/greivis-vasquez-nba-player-sports-diplomat/|access-date=17 June 2011|newspaper=[[The Baltimore Sun]]|date=15 June 2011}} ===New Orleans Hornets (2011–2013)=== On December 24, 2011, Vásquez was traded to the [[New Orleans Hornets]] in exchange for [[Quincy Pondexter]].{{cite web | url = http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets_acquire_greivis_vasque_2011_12_25.html | title = HORNETS ACQUIRE GREIVIS VASQUEZ | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = 2011-12-24 | access-date = 2011-12-25}} On February 1, 2012, against the [[Phoenix Suns]], Vasquez recorded 20 points and 12 assists off the bench. Vasquez received his first set of starts for the Hornets after a sore knee injury to Hornets guard [[Jarrett Jack]]. Vasquez received the starting job as point guard for the Hornets in the [[2012–13 NBA season]]. On November 23, 2012, Vasquez tallied 25 points and 14 assists (both career highs) in a loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]]. On January 1, 2013, Vasquez earned Western Conference Player of the Week honors. On February 8, 2013, in the game against the [[Atlanta Hawks]], Vasquez scored 21 points, along with 12 assists and 11 rebounds to secure his first career NBA [[triple-double]].{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/103543661/hornets-catch-hawks-off-guard/ |title=Hornets catch Hawks off-guard |author= |work=[[Anderson Independent-Mail]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] Vasquez|work=NBA.com|date=November 9, 2016|access-date=November 9, 2016}} ==Venezuela's National Team career== After winning at the U-15 level in 2003, Vásquez was called up for the U-21 Venezuelan NT for the 2004 U-21 Americas Tournament being four years under the tournament's age. Those were his only appearances on the youth national team setup. Vásquez made his Senior National Team debut in 2007 during the 2007 FIBA Americas Championship in Las Vegas while being a sophomore at the [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|University of Maryland]]. He was the second leading scorer of his squad averaging 12.1 points per game, third in rebounds with 4.1 per game and second best in assists with 3.3 Ast per contest. Venezuela finished 8th (2–6 record) out of 10 ten participating teams. His ascent was headlined during the 2011 FIBA Americas Championship, where he carried the Venezuelan team to a 5th-place finish. Already an NBA player, Vásquez was the second best scorer of the tournament with 19.3 PPG and first in assists with 5.8 APG. ==Coaching career== On August 15, 2019, the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] announced that Vásquez would serve as the associate head coach for the [[Birmingham Squadron|Erie BayHawks]].{{cite
